notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached, no hardware run is claimed, and the real MuJoCo engine and the sim backend were not run. The clone at the pinned commit 931f26f267386a83669bc8b937404824dfa21021 is unmodified.

CARD AND SHAPE: the card is family-config with helper MujocoDriver, role sim-env, expected_mode simulated and risk_floor R0. The card's entry symbols were confirmed in the read-only clone: mujoco_env/y_env.py:13 defines the concrete SimpleEnv and mujoco_env/y_env2.py:13 defines the concrete SimpleEnv2; SimpleEnv constructs MuJoCoParserClass from xml_path (mujoco_env/y_env.py:27). No helper deviation was needed. The package serves the card's models[0], asset/robotis_omy/scene.xml, through MujocoDriver; that scene includes asset/robotis_omy/omy.xml. The card's models[1] is the included robot model, not a second device, and is not served separately. The example scenes are not served: asset/example_scene_y.xml and asset/example_scene_y2.xml reference asset/objaverse/plate_11/model_new.xml, whose directory is absent until the README's unzip step, so the self-contained scene.xml is the served model.

INTERFACE: cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [10 numbers]}} and cap.world.reset.v1 takes {seed}. The MuJoCo bridge writes the ten control values to data.ctrl after checking each against the model's effective actuator_ctrlrange, then calls mj_step once per tick; reset calls mj_resetData + mj_forward and does not use the seed. The card's wrappers expose a seven-element joint action (six targets plus one gripper command, with the gripper command repeated four times and elements 1 and 3 scaled by 0.8 at mujoco_env/y_env.py:129-137); the package serves the model's own ten-element primary step interface one level below that wrapper, six arm position targets in radians and four gripper targets. The wrapper's GLFW viewer, teleoperation, reward/termination logic and camera helpers are not part of the MuJoCo family contract.

LIMITS AND UNITS: the driver declares no Limit. The bridge derives action.ctrl[0..9] from the model: the six arm actuators inherit ctrlrange -6.28319 to 6.28319 from default class Y at asset/robotis_omy/omy.xml:10, and the four gripper actuators declare 0..1.1, 0..1, 0..1.1 and 0..1 at asset/robotis_omy/omy.xml:114-117. All ten actuators have a control range, so there is no operator_required bound and no site-limits.example.json. The arm joints and actuator targets are in radians; the gripper ranges are the model's joint/actuator units. The bridge state is time_ms, qpos (10), qvel (10), ctrl (10), tick, timestep_ms and seed. The model sets no <option timestep>, so the fake and the F1 fidelity note use MuJoCo's 2 ms library default as a declared placeholder, not a line of the clone.

FAKE: backends['fake'] is the package's class object FakeMujoco, a stand-in for the mujoco library, not a recording and not the upstream simulator. It parses scene.xml and its omy.xml include for the ten hinge joints, the ten position actuators, the effective class-default ctrlranges and the option timestep, then integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control value. It loads no mesh, texture, contact or camera and runs no MuJoCo physics; fidelity_by_backend['fake'] publishes the F0 contract and its gaps. It returns 10-length qpos/qvel/ctrl arrays (no array is reduced). NOT COVERED: the camera frames of SimpleEnv.grab_image (agentview, egocentric, sideview); the served scene has only the wrist egocentric camera and the MuJoCo bridge publishes qpos/qvel/ctrl/time, not images. NOT COVERED: the tutorial's reward/termination/check_success logic, the language-conditioned SimpleEnv2 scene and the policy deployment notebooks. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used.

WARNINGS kept from the last gate run (all expected for simulator families, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake is a class-object stand-in for the mujoco library rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder, so native calls are not recorded and G7 has no fake class surface to check; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds eight cases (model shape from the card model, control-vector length, model-envelope refusal with zero effect, step advancing the integration state, reset to the model defaults, F0 fidelity publication, e-stop latch, and entry-symbol existence in the read-only clone); G9 passed. No human review or hardware test is claimed; the upstream licence is NOASSERTION/unknown and publication review is still required.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Model review confirmed the ten-actuator robot MJCF, inherited arm ranges, gripper ranges and both wrapper entries against the pinned clone. Edited driver.py and facts.md to correct fact ranges, identify robot-and-floor scope, and distinguish wrapper target staging from integration. Clarified that the latch retains ctrl and only a new explicit step resumes targets; test_driver.py now verifies this through the served fake. Regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the fake gate and strict collector pass. No real engine was run. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Owner publication decision remains required for NOASSERTION. The served model is the card's robot-and-floor scene, without the tutorial task objects or camera contract. Real MuJoCo compilation and mesh resolution were not tested; the 2 ms default remains an outside-clone assumption. E-stop retains targets and reset only unlatches.
